title: Interfacial control of magnetism and electron transport in nonisostructural SrRuO$_3$/SrCuO$_2$ heterostructure
authors: Digbijaya Palai, B. Maharana, P. Biswal, Shwetha G. Bhat, D. Nayak, D. Sahoo, R. Soni, K. Senapati, Z. Hossain, D. Samal
abstract: Heterointerfaces between structurally dissimilar oxides provide a platform to exploit the interfacial mismatch in the lattice and electronic degrees of freedom to realize emergent functionalities and tunable physical properties with potential applications in oxide electronics. Here, we investigate the magnetic and electronic transport properties of symmetry-mismatched SrRuO$_3$ (SRO)/SrCuO$_2$ (SCO) heterostructure, in which a 4-nm-thick itinerant ferromagnetic metal SRO is interfaced with a planar-type antiferromagnetic insulator SCO, in comparison with a reference SRO (4 nm) film. While both the bare SRO and SRO/SCO bilayer exhibit perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), the SRO/SCO bilayer shows a pronounced enhancement in the saturation magnetization (M$_S$ $\approx$ 2.7 $μ_B$/Ru) and effective anisotropy constant (K$_{\mathrm{eff}}$ $\approx$ 2.13 $\times$ 10$^6$ erg/cc) relative to the bare SRO film (M$_S$ $\approx$ 1.3 $μ_B$/Ru and K$_{\mathrm{eff}}$ $\approx$ 5.25 $\times$ 10$^5$ erg/cc). Interestingly, the low-temperature resistivity upturn below 5 K arising from disorder-induced quantum corrections in bare SRO is strongly suppressed in SRO/SCO, and it exhibits Fermi-liquid-like transport ($ρ\propto T^2$) down to 2 K. Analysis of the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) reveals dominant intrinsic Berry-curvature driven electron transport in both samples, with enhanced intrinsic and skew-scattering contributions in the SRO/SCO bilayer, indicating the critical role of the interface in modifying the electronic band structure near the Fermi level. Our results demonstrate that the interface acts as an effective control knob, concurrently enhancing the magnetization, PMA, and intrinsic scattering contribution to the AHE in the SRO/SCO heterostructure, while suppressing the disorder-driven quantum corrections to transport behavior observed in the bare SRO film.
summary: The study investigates the $	ext{SrRuO}_3/	ext{SrCuO}_2$ heterostructure to control magnetism and electron transport by exploiting structural mismatch. The interface acts as a critical knob, significantly boosting magnetization and anisotropy while simultaneously stabilizing the electronic state against disorder-induced quantum scattering. This confirms that interfacial engineering is a powerful tool for realizing novel functionalities in oxide electronics.
main_problem: The study investigates how structural mismatch at an interface can be used to control both the magnetic ordering and the electronic transport properties in oxide heterostructures.
main_result: The nonisostructural SrRuO3/SrCuO2 interface significantly enhances magnetization and perpendicular magnetic anisotropy while simultaneously suppressing low-temperature disorder-induced resistivity upturns, leading to Fermi-liquid behavior.
method: The research combines structural characterization (XRD, XRR) with comprehensive measurements of magnetism (SQUID-VSM) and electronic transport (resistivity $\rho(T)$ and Anomalous Hall Effect analysis).
model_or_system: The physical system is a heterostructure composed of an itinerant ferromagnetic metal ($	ext{SrRuO}_3$) interfaced with a planar antiferromagnetic insulator ($	ext{SrCuO}_2$). The interface forces structural changes, such as $\text{RuO}_6$ octahedral to $\text{RuO}_5$ pyramidal coordination.
key_observables: Saturation magnetization ($M_S$), effective anisotropy constant ($K_{	ext{eff}}$), temperature-dependent resistivity ($ho(T)$), and the anomalous Hall coefficient ($ eta$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (down to 2 K) are crucial for observing quantum corrections; enhanced $M_S$ ($\approx 2.7 \mu_B/\text{Ru}$) and $K_{	ext{eff}}$ enhancement are key metrics.
main_assumptions: The observed changes in transport properties (e.g., suppression of $\rho(T)$ upturn) are directly attributable to the interfacial electronic structure modification, such as charge transfer stabilizing a high-spin state.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD scans confirming structural quality; magnetization loops demonstrate enhanced $M_S$ and PMA in the bilayer; resistivity plots compare bare SRO (showing low-T upturn) versus SRO/SCO (showing $\rho \propto T^2$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence: first, structural confirmation of the interface; second, magnetic measurements showing enhancement; third, transport analysis demonstrating suppression of quantum corrections and enhanced AHE contributions.
why_interesting: This work demonstrates how engineered interfaces can act as powerful tuners for fundamental electronic properties in strongly correlated oxides, offering insights into interfacial charge transfer mechanisms that are relevant to emergent phenomena in condensed matter physics.
